title: P2.12b Enforce MCP allowlists on direct calls
description: Measured at HEAD 731bba1072c548854eb4bede782c35656edc983c: HTTP and stdio tools/list filter through allowlistedToolEntries, but tools/call in packages/mcp/src/http/http-tool-bridge.ts and packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-server.ts still resolve through the global STDIO_TOOL_INDEX. A client can directly invoke a valid generated tool omitted from its server allowlist. Bind both transport handlers to the exact construction-time entry set without changing tool vocabulary or concurrent events.resume work.
definitionOfDone: Re-measure exact owned paths and production call/list edges before editing; if any named path becomes foreign dirty or assigned elsewhere, record the collision and block rather than overwrite it.

For both Streamable HTTP and stdio, a direct tools/call for a generated tool omitted from the configured allowlist refuses CAPABILITY_DENIED with MCP code -32002 before authenticate or dispatch; a completely unknown label remains INPUT_INVALID.

tools/list and tools/call are driven by the same construction-time allowed entry set. With no allowlist, the existing full generated list and valid direct calls remain byte-for-byte behaviorally compatible.

Add real SDK/transport parity coverage over exactly two transports. Pin a nonzero exact denominator, exact code/layer-equivalent runtime payload, and zero recording-port calls for an omitted known tool; include positive allowed and unknown-label controls.

Mutation drill: restore global-index-only direct resolution in each transport separately, prove the corresponding test goes red, restore tracked bytes exactly, then run package typecheck/tests plus path-attributed root regression. Commit only explicit owned paths.
